description: We are a team of four high school students passionate about science, technology, and understanding our planet. As part of the “Be An Earth System Trend Detective” challenge, we aim to explore NASA’s Earth science data, identify environmental patterns and trends, and turn scientific information into meaningful insights. Through teamwork, curiosity, and creativity, we hope to better understand changes in Earth’s systems and contribute to a more sustainable future.
summary:
RainDetect Türkiye is an interactive website that explores how rainfall has changed across all 81 provinces of Türkiye between 2000 and 2025.We used NASA POWER precipitation data to create a platform where users can select a province, explore historical rainfall charts, compare regions, and view changes on an interactive map.To identify rainfall trends, we used the Theil–Sen estimator and the Mann–Kendall test. These methods help us measure the direction of change and distinguish statistically significant trends from ordinary year-to-year variability.
Our website also includes a year-by-year rainfall animation, allowing users to see how precipitation patterns differ across Türkiye.We developed RainDetect Türkiye to make NASA Earth science data easier to understand and to encourage students and the public to explore environmental changes through real scientific data.
details:
About Our Project

We created RainDetect Türkiye to investigate how rainfall patterns have changed across Türkiye over the last 26 years. We wanted to understand whether different provinces show similar trends or whether rainfall changes vary from region to region.

Our website covers all 81 provinces and uses annual precipitation data from NASA POWER for the years 2000–2025.

How It Works

Users can select a province and view its historical rainfall data through an interactive chart. The website also displays the estimated precipitation trend and its statistical significance.

We used the Theil–Sen estimator to calculate the rate of change in rainfall and the Mann–Kendall test to evaluate whether the observed trend is statistically significant.

Our interactive map shows geographical differences in precipitation trends. We also developed a year-by-year animation that allows users to explore how rainfall varied across Türkiye between 2000 and 2025.

The province comparison section makes it easier to examine differences between regions.

Tools and Technologies

We built our website using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. We used Leaflet for interactive mapping and GitHub Pages to publish the website.

Our main scientific data source is NASA POWER, using MERRA-2-based precipitation data.

During development, we also used Claude and ChatGPT as supporting tools for coding assistance, debugging, and improving written explanations. Our team reviewed and organized the final project.

Why Our Project Matters

Rainfall affects agriculture, water resources, ecosystems, and everyday life. Türkiye has different geographical and climatic conditions, so rainfall changes may not follow the same pattern in every province.

We wanted to create a tool that makes these differences easier to explore using real scientific data.

Our website helps users understand that a single dry or wet year does not necessarily represent a long-term trend. Statistical analysis is important when interpreting environmental change.

Limitations

The NASA POWER data represent gridded environmental estimates, not rainfall measurements from every location within each province. We use one representative point per province, so local variations may not be fully captured.

Our analysis focuses on annual precipitation totals and does not predict future rainfall.

Future Improvements

In the future, we would like to add temperature analysis, seasonal precipitation comparisons, longer historical records, and more advanced statistical methods.

We hope RainDetect Türkiye can help students and the public become more interested in Earth science and environmental data.
